## Source and method

- https://developer.android.com/health-and-fitness/health-connect/data-types

Every record class in Google's Health Connect data-types table (https://developer.android.com/health-and-fitness/health-connect/data-types), read on 2026-10-03, joined to each class's Jetpack reference page. Class name, category, record shape, unit class, mandatory fields and the read/write permission strings are copied from Google's data-types table; the permission evidence column keeps the table text the strings were read from. Aggregate metrics, availability, feature flags and the description are copied from the Jetpack reference. Nothing is inferred: a field Google's pages do not state is null. Where Google's own pages disagree (the data-types table and the HealthPermissions reference spell one exercise-route permission differently), the record page shows both readings; this dataset carries the data-types table's string.

## Fields

| Field | Description | JSON types | Null in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `className` | Jetpack record class name | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `qualifiedName` | Not described in the dataset's fields dictionary. | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `dataType` | Not described in the dataset's fields dictionary. | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `category` | Google's category for the data type, as printed on the data-types page | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `recordShape` | Interval, Instantaneous or Series, per Google's table | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `unitClass` | Unit class Google's table names; null where none | null, string | 27 of 42 rows |
| `mandatoryFields` | Fields Google's table lists as mandatory, semicolon-separated | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `readPermissions` | android.permission.health read strings for the class, semicolon-separated | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `writePermissions` | android.permission.health write strings for the class, semicolon-separated | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `permissionEvidence` | The table text the permission strings were read from | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `aggregateMetrics` | AggregateMetric constants on the class, semicolon-separated; null where none | null, string | 18 of 42 rows |
| `addedIn` | Availability as the Jetpack reference prints it | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `featureFlag` | Not described in the dataset's fields dictionary. | null, string | 38 of 42 rows |
| `deprecated` | Not described in the dataset's fields dictionary. | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `description` | The first paragraph of Google's class description, verbatim | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `googleDocs` | Google's Jetpack reference page the row was read from | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `sourceUpdated` | That page's "Last updated" date | string | 0 of 42 rows |
| `page` | This site's page for the record | string | 0 of 42 rows |

A null means the source does not state the value or it could not be verified. It never means zero, and it is never a guess. In the CSV a null is an empty unquoted field.

## Update cadence

- `src/data/healthConnectRecords.ts` is generated by `scripts/fetch-health-connect-records.mjs` from the sources above, last read 2026-10-03.
- No workflow runs that script: it is run by hand when the sources are re-read.
- The files are rebuilt by `npm run datasets` (scripts/build-datasets.mjs); a run with no source change writes byte-identical files. The edition stays 2026.1, and a new edition ships under a new file name rather than overwriting this one.
